title: Claim filed more than a year after the visit
summary: Medicare denied an office visit as filed too late (CO-29, N211). The claim was first sent 13 months after the visit, and the billing file shows no exception that would extend the deadline.

visit_note.text:
Date of visit: 2025-08-05
Patient: 77-year-old man, established patient.
Reason for visit: four days of increased breathlessness and cough with more sputum, now yellow.
History: COPD, former smoker (40 pack-years, quit 2015). Uses tiotropium daily and albuterol as needed, now four times a day.
Examination: temperature 37.6 C, respiratory rate 22, oxygen saturation 92% on room air. Scattered wheeze, no focal crackles. Blood pressure 138/84.
Assessment: acute exacerbation of COPD; hypertension controlled on lisinopril.
Plan: prednisone 40 mg daily for 5 days; doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 5 days; continue tiotropium. Return or go to the emergency department if breathing worsens. Review in two weeks.
Signed: treating physician. 2025-08-05.

supporting_documents.text:
Billing review for the visit of 2025-08-05.
The charge was found on the unbilled-encounters report during the month-end review on 2026-08-28. It had been held since 2025-08-06 by a practice-management edit for a missing diagnosis pointer, and the edit was never worked.
Clearinghouse acceptance report: first and only submission on 2026-09-01. No earlier submission of this claim is on file with the clearinghouse or the Medicare contractor.
Eligibility check on 2026-09-01: Medicare Part B entitlement effective 2013-07-01, with no retroactive change. No Medicare Advantage enrollment during 2025.
No correspondence from the Medicare contractor about this claim before the denial.
